recommendation: Keep the source fix. It removes stale normative guidance from a build-scoped Resource narrative without broadening the language starter set beyond the applied source history; future Common Languages additions should be handled by separate terminology-maintenance trackers.
issue_request: FHIR-39627 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to include commonly used European language tags in the Common Languages ValueSet to avoid warnings when IGs use them. The Jira discussion also recorded the accepted binding approach: Common Languages is a UI/starter set, while the actual language binding should be required to the full IETF/BCP-47 language value set.
initial_application: Commit ba6dd4995575f6af4f7f38c23835ffdbb250256d changed Resource.language and the Language binding row to a required binding on ValueSet/all-languages with ValueSet/languages as an additional starter binding. Commit 069c79bfb864dfd415b94ed50a9c1855d7aee10a added the EU language codes requested by the issue to source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml. No prior issue-specific commit updated source/resource/resource-notes.xml, which still described the old preferred-plus-maximum binding model.
additional_context: Resource is active in source/fhir.ini and source/resource/resource-notes.xml feeds the current Resource page narrative. Current active resource StructureDefinitions no longer bind language elements directly to ValueSet/languages without the all-languages binding, and later Common Languages maintenance left the starter ValueSet duplicate-free. InventoryItem still contains direct Common Languages bindings, but InventoryItem is no longer an active core resource in source/fhir.ini and now points to the OO incubator, so it was not edited for this current core reconciliation.
reconciliation: Changed source/resource/resource-notes.xml to say any valid BCP-47 language tag is valid through the required All Languages binding and that Common Languages is an additional starter binding for common UI choices. The commit intentionally did not add tr-TR to the starter ValueSet because Turkish is already represented by tr and the required All Languages binding permits tr-TR without warnings.
source_changes: source/resource/resource-notes.xml: replaced stale preferred/maximum binding prose with required All Languages plus additional starter Common Languages binding prose.

related_jiras.note: Later Common Languages ordering/duplicate cleanup audited the same ValueSet and confirmed the current starter list is duplicate-free and sorted, so no additional list cleanup was needed here.

Later Common Languages maintenance rewrote source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml while preserving the applied FHIR-39627 list, reinforcing that the remaining issue was stale Resource narrative text rather than missing current ValueSet maintenance.
